title.title: Lipschitz-equivalent separable spaces need not be isomorphic
title.subtitle: Claim: separable $X$, $Y$ are the same metric space up to bounded distortion, yet not linearly isomorphic

plain: Two spaces you can bend into each other with bounded stretching, yet no straight-line map matches them

object.axisLabel: the stretch $\|\Psi(s)-\Psi(t)\| \,/\, \|s-t\|$, over all pairs $s \ne t$

beats.text: A bijection $\Psi: X \to Y$ changes every distance by a bounded factor
The claimed $\Psi$ keeps every stretch between $4/21$ and $76/25$
Yet $X$ contains $c_0(\ell_2)$ isometrically and $Y$ has no linear copy of it

steps: Build a near-isometric bending of Hilbert space
Linearize it on the Lipschitz-free space
Assemble two graph spaces: only one contains $c_0(\ell_2)$

achievement.label: Aharoni–Lindenstrauss (1978); Kalton's Problem 3 (2008)
statement: X \sim_{\mathrm{Lip}} Y \not\Rightarrow X \cong Y \quad (X, Y \text{ separable})
achievement.context: Before: non-separable counterexamples (1978); $c_0$ is determined by its Lipschitz structure
achievement.note: Real scalars only; the obstruction is $c_0(\ell_2)$, not $c_0$

verify.detail: In Lean with the explicit $4/21$ and $76/25$ bounds, plus the $c_0$-absorption companion
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement's description; we did not build it

voice.text: A bijection stretching every distance by a bounded factor. Must the spaces then match linearly?
Bend Hilbert space slightly, linearize, and build two different graph spaces.
Claimed: not necessarily, even for separable spaces.

sources.quote: (4/21)||s-t|| <= ||Psi(s)-Psi(t)|| <= (76/25)||s-t||, where X contains a linearly isometric copy of c_0(l_2) but Y contains no linear copy of c_0(l_2)

sources.ref: article, Lipschitz-equivalent separable spaces need not be isomorphic
sources.quote: Aharoni and Lindenstrauss said no for huge non-separable spaces in 1978.

sources.ref: article, Lipschitz-equivalent separable spaces need not be isomorphic
sources.quote: Kalton listed it as Problem 3 in his 2008 survey

sources.ref: article, Lipschitz-equivalent separable spaces need not be isomorphic
sources.quote: Godefroy, Kalton and Lancien had shown $c_0$ is determined by its Lipschitz structure.
Real scalars only; no reflexive or complex analogue claimed. The obstruction is block-valued (c_0(l_2), not c_0).
